newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary cuts 1996 c/a deficit, output sluggish-KSH.
newsitem.headline: Hungary cuts 1996 c/a deficit, output sluggish-KSH.

text.p: Hungary has progressed in reducing the current account deficit in 1996 but had little success in boosting production, the central statistical office (KSH) said in a review.
"The deficit of the current account was $3.9 billion in 1994, $2.5 billion in 1995 and $1.7 billion in 1996," KSH said.

"In 1995, foreign trade played a key role in reducing the deficit, while in 1996...tourism had an excellent track record by almost doubling its revenue surplus from 1995 to $1.3 billion in 1996," it said.
The $1.7 billion current account deficit was covered by the inflow of working capital which amounted to $1.8 billion last year, it added.

However, production figures in Hungary's main industrial sectors showed mostly modest growth, stagnation or decline, it said, adding that investments showed a four-percent decline from the previous year.
Hungary's industrial output grew 2.3 percent last year, but growth was uneven.

Industry output increased 1.1 percent in the first half of 1996 over the same six months of 1995, grew 2.3 percent in the third quarter over Q3 1995 and was 4.3-percent higher in the October-December period over Q4 1995, KSH said.
Exports grew 13.5 percent, KSH said, adding "this is high even compared to international levels."
Construction industrial output fell 1.1 percent from 1995, but the pace of decline slowed in the second half of the year.
Agricultural output rose five percent, but this overall growth rate hid differences among the areas.
Consumer prices rose an average 23.6 percent in 1996 over 1995, while producer prices were 21.8- percent above the previous year.

Real wages fell 5.4 percent over the year. Gross monthly wages averaged 46,800 forints and net wages averaged 30,300 forints last year. -- Budapest newsroom +36 1 327-4040 ($ = 174.6 Hungarian Forints)
